## Glossary

**archive suggest**  
The CLI tagger: runSuggestions with the Haiku subscription runner.

**atlas:<concept>**  
Tag for the Atlas concept of repository files a session's tool calls touched.

**claudeDecisionModel**  
Internal: primed, text-only Claude Code sessions with no tools, forked per request.

**claudeSuggestModel**  
Internal Haiku 5.5 runner on the machine's Claude login; not exported.

**container root**  
A directory holding other projects' roots; naming it tags nothing.

**decision-runner**  
Class: the isolated, text-only Claude Code runner for model passes (internal).

**defaultIntegrations**  
The built-in GitHub and Linear integrations.

**integration**  
A source of references: GitHub and Linear natively, others by a literal link prefix.

**junk**  
The tagger's suggestion for empty, aborted, probe or accidental sessions.

**pool**  
Run an async function over items with at most N at once; N is required.

**project:<id>**  
Tag for each project whose roots hold a path the session accessed; search only, never routes.

**PROJECT_TAG_PREFIX**  
The constant 'project:'.

**provenance references**  
The session's recorded GitHub repository and branch.

**reference**  
A pointer {integration, ref} to an item such as owner/repo#24 or KEY-12.

**--refresh**  
Ask the tagger again for sessions already asked at this key.

**runSuggestions**  
Batch the due sessions through a caller-supplied model and record results.

**sessionDigest**  
The short view (counts, first prompts, tools, first and last replies) the tagger sees.

**shellAccess / toolCallAccess**  
Parse paths accessed and written by a shell script / one tool call.

**shellPaths / toolCallPaths**  
Paths accessed only, no writes.

**SUGGEST_PROMPT**  
The tagger's instruction text.

**suggestedTags**  
The tagger's suggestions (origin model); shown, never applied.

**suggestionKey**  
Hash of SUGGEST_PROMPT, model and tag definitions; a change makes sessions due again.

**tag**  
A concept label on an archive; a person's edit needs no revision and does not sync.

**tag definition**  
An offered category tag, archive-wide or for one actor (tags define).

**tagger**  
Class: the model tagger's queue, prompt, parser and runSuggestions; never applied automatically.

**tags-and-references**  
Class: tags, Atlas and project: tags, references, tag definitions and the path parser.

## 1. What this Warden covers

The archive's own labels and pointers: person-applied tags, Atlas and project: tags, integration references, the parser that reads which paths tool calls touched, the model tagger that only suggests, and the isolated text-only Claude runner the tagger and planner share.

## 2. The domain

Tags are concepts a person owns: collector --tags, atlas:<concept> from atlas graph --json (atlasTags), and tags people add with `archive tag` (ArchiveStore.tag, the `tag` action); tag edits need no new revision, survive re-capture and do not sync. project:<id> tags (PROJECT_TAG_PREFIX) name every project whose roots hold a path a session accessed, resolved by projectPaths over machineProjects with the longest root winning; they are for search only and never route or change a session's own project. References point at integration items: provenanceReferences turns recorded git context into GitHub references, archiveReferences lists a snapshot's references, referencesIn finds links in other text; a link is a mention, not proof of work. Which paths a call touched comes from toolCallAccess/toolCallPaths (a whole tool call) and shellAccess/shellPaths (a bare script); the Access variants also return writes.

The tagger suggests junk, up to three defined category tags and project:<id> for unrouted sessions; suggestions (suggestedTags) are never applied, and only a person applies one. From the shell, `archive suggest` runs it on Claude Haiku 5.5 through the machine's subscription. In code, runSuggestions (`@inixiative/archive/suggest`) takes a caller-supplied model: the Haiku runner (claudeSuggestModel) and claudeDecisionModel are internal to src/suggest-claude.ts and not exported, so only the CLI wires them together. suggestionKey hashes SUGGEST_PROMPT, the model and the tag definitions, so a session is asked once per digest and again only when one of those changes. pool runs work with a required concurrency (no default).

Not here: run tags, ARCHIVE_RUN, .archive-run and exempt sessions (what-an-archive-keeps); the per-entry write/read evidence and the machine project map as routing evidence (routing-organizations); the planner, claudeRouteModel and route:<organization> decisions (routing-planning); the HTTP tag and suggestion actions as endpoints (running-the-archive); the TagEdit, TagDefinition and Suggestion models (session-store).

**Source:** `README.md` § Tags and references (in "Archive")

#### Tags and references

The archive owns its tag system. It keeps two different things apart:

- **Tags** are concepts: the `atlas:<concept>` of repository files a session's tool calls touched (collectors with `--atlas`, from `atlas graph --json`), collector `--tag`s, and tags people add. **Suggestions** (`suggestedTags`) are the tagger's (`origin: "model"`, below) and are never applied. A person applies one with `tag --tag`; tags a person applied or removed never show as suggestions.
- **Run tags** mark sessions that are not a person's work: `run:test` (tests, probes), `run:oracle` (Oracle and bench evaluations) and `run:foundry` (sessions Foundry starts itself: Wardens, the chorus, middleware roles, classifiers). The harness that runs a session stamps it explicitly, one of three ways: a run tag on the snapshot it writes (or `collect --tag`); `ARCHIVE_RUN=test|oracle|foundry` in the environment of a process that writes snapshots (Foundry, `archive import`); or a `.archive-run` file holding the run kind in the working directory the runner made, or an ancestor (`stampRunDirectory` in `@inixiative/archive/exemption`), which collectors read at capture. A marker counts only below every collector root: one at the filesystem root, the home directory, or at or above a collector root is ignored, so a stray file never stamps a project's sessions, and `stampRunDirectory` refuses those places and a git work tree's root. Foundry's own subagents are `run:foundry` by the agent type Claude Code records for them (`foundry-root`, `foundry-dispatch`, `foundry-warden`: in-session Wardens inside a person's session; `d-`/`w-` and 16 hex digits: its decision hosts); Foundry refuses those types to anyone else, so a person's subagents (`general-purpose`, `Explore`, …) are never caught. *Interim, until every fixture and runner stamps:* the archive also infers `run:test` from Foundry's test fixture identities (project `P`, the `watch-A`/`watch-B` threads) and from working directories (temp directories, scratchpads, `decision-receipts`), `run:foundry` from Foundry's primed hosts (`decision-receipts/primed-<host>/fixture`), and `run:oracle` from Oracle eval workspaces, `.oracle` and bench run checkouts; the collector writes `run:inferred` beside a tag it guessed from a directory. Inferences only exempt: they never make a session one an Archive drops. These guesses go once the stamps cover them. An ACP thread (`acp`, `acp:<client>`) is a person's Foundry session from Zed, T3 or Paseo, never a run. A session captured before 0.23.0 with an inferred run tag lacks `run:inferred` and reads as explicitly stamped; re-capture it (`archive repair`) before turning `captureRunSessions` off. A session captured earlier keeps its tags until it is captured again. Whether run sessions are kept at all is the `captureRunSessions` setting (below). A kept, exempt session feeds nothing that learns from sessions: suggestions, retention scoring, correction mining (`foundry repeats`) or agent context. `list` and `search` leave exempt sessions out unless asked (`exempt: "include"` or `"only"`); routing and sync still see every session. Removing the run tag (`tag --untag run:test`) lifts the exemption.
- **Project tags** name the projects a session worked in, not where it lives, and are for search only (routing follows plans): a collector tags each session (subagents included) `project:<projectId>` for every project whose roots or worktrees, in any collector of `agents.json` and of either source, hold a path it accessed: its working directory, the path arguments of file tools (Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, notebooks), the path arguments, `cd` and `git -C` targets of shell commands (Claude Code's Bash; Codex's exec_command, shell and `exec` cells, best effort), Codex patch file headers and a call's `workdir`. Mentions never count: text written by Write or Edit, heredoc bodies, quoted strings with spaces, subagent prompts, messages, and user or assistant prose. Relative paths resolve against the working directory (and a `cd` before them); the longest root wins, and a project's own root counts even when it holds its own worktrees. Naming a container root itself, one that holds other projects' roots (`ls ~/code/inixiative`), tags nothing. It reads the raw transcript, before any tool-activity strip, and never changes the session's own project: an org-level session (cwd `~/code/inixiative`) stays in its project and carries `project:kingdom`, `project:template` and the rest it touched. The tagger's `project:` suggestion for an unrouted session is a different thing: where it belongs.
- **References** point at items in an integration. Collectors record the session's GitHub repository and branch (`owner/repo`, `owner/repo/tree/branch`); linked GitHub pull requests, issues and commits (`owner/repo#24`, `owner/repo@sha`) and Linear issues (`KEY-12`) are found in the text and counted. A link is a mention, not proof of work. The archive's settings list the integrations it references: GitHub and Linear are recognized natively, and any other integration names the link prefix of its items (for example `https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/`); the item is what follows. Prefixes are literal, so settings cannot make matching slow.

```sh
bun run archive tag --id ARCHIVE_ID --tag reviewed --untag debugging
```

<!-- unit doc:README.md#the-tagger -->
**Source:** `README.md` § The tagger (in "Archive")

#### The tagger

The **tagger** suggests, for every session that is not exempt: `junk` (empty, aborted, probes, accidental starts), up to three of the archive-wide category tags (`tags define`), and `project:<id>` when the session landed `unrouted` or without a project. It runs on the machine's Claude subscription: Claude Haiku 5.5 on primed, text-only Claude Code sessions from `@inixiative/agent-session` (no tools, MCP servers, user settings or instruction files; an API-key login is refused). The model judges every due session, in batches of short digests (counts, the first prompts, tools used, first and last replies), never whole transcripts; nothing is decided by keyword or size rules first. The only skip: a session is asked about once per digest, and is due again only when it changes or when the prompt, model or tag definitions do (`--refresh` asks again, for example after adding a project). Suggestions for an older digest are not shown. It reads only this machine's Archive, since session content goes to this machine's Claude login. Each run prints its calls and tokens.

```sh
bun run archive tags define --tag debugging --description "Diagnosing and fixing a failure"
bun run archive suggest [--limit N] [--batch 8] [--concurrency 2] [--refresh]
bun run archive list --suggested junk
bun run archive list --exempt only
```

Tag edits apply to that archive without a new revision, survive re-capture, and do not sync. Offered tags are defined archive-wide or for one actor.
